title: Human Behavior-Informed Crash Scenario Generation with Real-World Crash Priors for Autonomous Vehicle Safety Evaluation

control_signal.value: A retrieved real-world crash prior, matched to the current scene, that gives an anchor trajectory for a candidate adversarial vehicle plus behavior-stage timings (risk, emergency, collision); a VLM agent picks the adversary.

control_mechanism.value: Gradient-based clean guidance in the last reverse DDIM steps: a differentiable loss on decoded trajectories (anchor, stage, collision, realism, route terms) modifies the noise prediction with scale s.

base_model.value: Scene-conditioned latent diffusion model with interaction-aware graph encoder and decoder, temporal U-Net denoiser, kinematic-bicycle propagation; plus a VLM scene-understanding agent and crash-prior retrieval.

datasets.value: Diffusion model trained on nuScenes training split; real-world crash data used as priors; builds nuCrash (over 4,000 crash and near-crash scenarios) from nuScenes scenes; SimEngine as comparison dataset.

metrics.value: Crash and near-crash rates, TV distance and JSD between generated and real crash-type distributions, emergency-response stage proportion and pre-impact timing; planner closed-loop safety metrics.

controllability_evidence.value: Ablation: removing crash-prior retrieval cuts the emergency-response proportion from 22% to 12%, further from the real-world 32%. CrashSim has the smallest TV and JSD to real crash distributions.

stated_limitations.value: LLM-based evaluation attributes failure mechanisms only coarsely; CrashSim needs broader real-world crash databases and more reactive modelling of surrounding traffic.

notes: Guidance is driven by retrieved priors rather than a user-specified attribute; no controllability metric reported in this packet beyond realism/distribution match and ablation. Real-world crash database name not in packet.
